item.title: Chad's government says it's withdrawing from the ICC
item.description: Chad's Foreign Ministry has announced plans to leave the International Criminal Court. It said that its effectiveness was "limited and uneven." Chad's leader is a military officer accused of repressing the opposition.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Indian youth score a win over Modi with humor and grit
item.description: Driven by social media satire, the Gen-Z-led "Cockroach" protest movement spurned by grievances over an exam scandal caused a shake-up in India's government. DW spoke with a few protesters in New Delhi.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ghana's community service bill: A fix for the prison crisis?
item.description: The community service bill offers community service as an alternative to prison sentences, particularly for minor offenses. It's meant to decongest Ghana's prisons and prevent overcrowding once it's signed into law.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Fujimori takes charge in Peru amid China, US balancing act
item.description: Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. As she takes office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: How India's Gen-Z protesters shifted the political debate
item.description: The resignation of India's education minister amounts to a stunning victory for the youth-led "Cockroach" protest movement. The bigger question is if this political momentum turns into a lasting platform for more reform.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Berlin Pride attack: What we know so far
item.description: On Saturday, a vehicle drove into a crowd near a Christopher Street Day celebration in what is being regarded as an attack on the LGBTQ+ community. The main suspect has since been confronted and shot dead.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Berlin Pride: Latest in string of deadly vehicle attacks
item.description: The attack at a Berlin Pride event is only the most recent incident on a long list where vehicles were used as weapons. The US, Canada, and China also saw similar attacks in recent years.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can Pakistan-administered Kashmir elections calm tensions?
item.description: Pakistan-administered Kashmir heads to the polls after weeks of deadly protests over seats reserved for displaced people from India-administered Kashmir. One local group has called for the elections to be boycotted.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Sudan civil war: Civilians used as 'human shields'
item.description: The situation in the besieged city of El Obeid in Sudan is worsening by the day, with rights organizations warning of mass atrocities. Children are traumatized and do not dare go to school.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Brazil denies entry to senior Trump officials ahead of elections
item.description: Brazil rejected visas for two planned US envoys, alleging that Washington was seeking to shape Brazil's upcoming presidential election. The development adds to a deepening political tension between Brazil and the US.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Serbia's LGBTQ+ community faces 'epidemic of violence'
item.description: Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
item.description: Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.
